chunks: From him, from Ibn Fazzal, and Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, some people in Al-Madina said, 'Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) has no wealth.' So Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) sent for a man in Al-Madina, borrowed a thousand dirhams from him, and sent it to the collector (of khums/charity), saying, 'This is the charity of our wealth.' So they said, 'Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) would not have sent this from himself except that he indeed has wealth.'

key_terms.الْحَسَنُ ( عليه السلام ): Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Al-Hasan ibn Ali
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: Al-Madina (the city, often referring to Kufa or Medina in historical contexts)
key_terms.تِلْقَاءِ نَفْسِهِ: From himself / on his own authority
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: Dirham, a silver coin used as currency
key_terms.صَدَقَةُ: Charity (specifically referring to the giving of wealth for religious purposes)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Al-Hasan (AS) prove he had wealth when people thought he was poor?
ai.summary: This narrative, recorded in *Al-Kafi*, highlights Imam Al-Hasan’s (peace be upon him) strategic use of *hiyal* (legal stratagems) to preserve the dignity of the Imams and clarify their financial status for religious obligations like *khums*. By borrowing a sum and immediately donating it as *sadaqah*, he demonstrated that his apparent lack of visible wealth was not due to poverty but rather to its concealment or specific form, thereby validating his eligibility to receive and distribute religious dues. This act underscores the Shia scholarly understanding of the Imams' economic independence and their role in maintaining the integrity of the *khums* system.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ibn Fazzal, and Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The people in Al-Medina were saying, ‘There is no wealth for Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>’.

So Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> sent for a man of Al-Medina and borrowed a thousand Dirhams from him, and sent with it to the governor and said: ‘This is a charity of our<sup>asws</sup> wealth’. So they said, ‘Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> would not have sent this from himself<sup>asws</sup> except that there was indeed wealth for him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ibn Faddal and ibn Mahbub from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that in al-Madinah people said, ‘Al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, has no assets . 5

Al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, sent to a man in al-Madinah, borrowed one thousand dirham from him and sent it to the charity collector saying, ‘It is the charity due on our assets . 5 People said, ‘Al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has not sent it without a reason. This is because of a certain amount of assets ."
